### Patients and Methods

#### Study Design

We performed a retrospective, before-and-after study in a 54-bed children's hospital within Sanford Medical Center (Fargo, ND), a tertiary care hospital. The study was conducted from November 1, 2012 to April 1, 2015. We compared hospitalization rates for RSV in the 2 seasons before (2012–2013 and 2013–2014) and the season after (2014–2015) implementing a change in palivizumab administration practices in accordance with the 2014 AAP guideline. We defined the RSV season as beginning on November 1 and ending on April 1st. RSV hospitalization was defined as one of the following items documented in the medical record during hospital admission: positive RSV rapid antigen test, or positive RSV reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction test.

#### Ethics

The study was approved by the institutional review board with a waiver of informed consent and performed in accordance with the ethical standards of the 1964 Declaration of Helsinki and its later amendments.

#### Inclusion and Exclusion Criteria

Hospitalized patients younger than 2 years of age from the 2012–2013 and 2013–2014 RSV seasons were included in the pre-2014 guideline group: November 1, 2012 to April 1, 2013 and November 1, 2013 to April 1, 2014. Hospitalized patients younger than 2 years of age from the 2014–2015 RSV season were included in the post-2014 guideline group: November 1, 2014 to April 1, 2015. To ensure that hospitalization was not related to routine birth at our medical center, initial screening was not performed on hospitalized patients born within our medical center who had never been discharged home. Likewise, patients were excluded if they were admitted as an inpatient transfer from a referring hospital during their initial birth hospitalization (Fig. 1).

#### Palivizumab Administration

Eligibility for palivizumab receipt at Sanford Medical Center Fargo was evaluated at birth or at first clinic visit by nursing staff using an institutionally developed screening tool. All medical centers and clinic sites within the Fargo region of our health system utilize this tool. During the pre-2014 guideline period, the screening tool adherered to the 2012 AAP palivizumab guideline (Appendix A, Supplemental Digital Content 1, [https://links.lww.com/INF/C443](https://links.lww.com/INF/C443)). The screening tool was altered in 2014 to adhere to the 2014 AAP palivizumab guideline (Appendix B, Supplemental Digital Content 2, [https://links.lww.com/INF/C444](https://links.lww.com/INF/C444)). The revised screening tool was in use before the start of the RSV season. During the entire study period, eligible neonates were administered their first dose of palivizumab before leaving the hospital with the remaining doses given as outpatients in their local clinic.

#### Patient Data Collection

We collected the following information for each patient from the electronic medical record: age, sex, length of stay, race, insurance information, RSV laboratory test results and gestational age at birth. International Classification of Diseases, Ninth Revision codes for RSV bronchiolitis (079.6) or codes related to RSV (466.11, 480.1 and V04.82) were also collected for all hospitalized patients, and utilized as a subsequent assessment to ensure that no laboratory data related to RSV was missing.

#### RSV Assays

Patients with acute respiratory symptoms were evaluated for RSV disease upon admission at the discretion of the provider. The diagnosis of RSV required laboratory confirmation, and results of all ordered RSV laboratory tests were reviewed for each child included in the study. Testing was performed using BinaxNOW RSV immunochromatographic assays to detect RSV fusion protein antigen in nasopharyngeal swabs (93% sensitivity, 93% specificity, Alere Scarborough Inc., Scarborough, ME) or Simplexa Flu A/B & RSV Direct Reverse Transcriptase Polymerase Chain Reaction Assays (95% sensitivity, 95% specificity, Focus Diagnostics, Cypress, CA).

#### Palivizumab Administration Data

We queried our electronic database for all doses of palivizumab administered in our medical center and at the clinics within our health system located in the surrounding counties served (Appendix C, Supplemental Digital Content 3, [https://links.lww.com/INF/C445](https://links.lww.com/INF/C445)). All clinic and hospital locations within our health system utilize the same electronic medical record.

#### Outcomes

The primary outcome was hospitalization for laboratory-confirmed RSV expressed as a rate per 1000 children <24 months. To calculate rates, the denominator for each RSV season was the total number of live births in the previous 24 months from the start of the applicable RSV season (November 1), similar to other investigations of this nature.[[11](javascript:void(0);)] The secondary outcome investigated was total doses of palivizumab administered during each respiratory season corrected for number of children <24 months.

#### Birth Cohorts

To facilitate calculation of incidence rates of RSV hospitalizations per 1000 children <24 months, number of live births was collected from the North Dakota and Minnesota departments of health for 2 years before the start of each RSV season. Births from Cass County, ND (county of residence for our medical center), Clay County, MN, and surrounding counties with at least 20 births occurring at the study center were included (Appendix C, Supplemental Digital Content 3, [https://links.lww.com/INF/C445](https://links.lww.com/INF/C445)).

#### Statistical Analysis

A pre-analysis power calculation demonstrated that with an assigned α value of 0.05, a total birth cohort of 34,000 would yield 80% power to detect a difference of 2.5 RSV hospitalizations for every 1000 children <24 months (e.g., an increase from 5 per 1000 children <24 months to 7.5 per 1000 children <24 months). The total birth cohort of 34,000 would be the sum of the total number of children less than 24 months of age at the start of each RSV season observed. Categorical variables were summarized as frequency (%). Pearson χ 2 tests were used to compare differences in baseline characteristics between groups. Incidence rates for the primary outcome were calculated by dividing the number of RSV hospitalizations for children younger than two years of age by the number of total live births occurring within 2 years of the start of the corresponding RSV season. For the primary outcome of RSV hospitalizations, confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated by assuming a Poisson distribution, and rates were compared using the Student's _t_ test. Trend of RSV hospitalizations by month during each RSV season was descriptive and not analyzed statistically. A _P_ value of <0.05 was considered statistically significant. All analyses were performed using JMP software, version 12.0.1 (Cary, NC) and MedCalc statistical software version 15.4 (Ostend, Belgium).

**Program: Miners' Hospital**

**_Function_**

Within the University Hospital is the Miner's Hospital. At the time of Statehood, Congress granted 100,000 acres of land to the State of Utah for the hospital. The School and Institutional Trust Lands was established to be administered by the State. One of the stipulations under the original agreement was that the proceeds from the sale of the lands were to be used to fund a hospital for disabled miners. In 1957, Legislation established a Rehabilitation Center from the revenues from the trust fund to be used to build a Miners' Hospital. This program provides healthcare for disabled miners including outreach programs, seminars, and screening services. In addition, the hospital has established two scholarships for the children or grandchildren of disabled miners.

**_Statutory Authority_**

The following laws govern the operations of the University and Miner's Hospital in addition to the laws previously mentioned:

*   [UCA 53C-1-101](http://www.le.utah.gov/UtahCode/getCodeSection?code=53C-1-101) is the School and Institutional Trust Lands Management Act which administers the revenue from the sale of the lands to be used to fund a hospital for disabled miners. 
*   [UCA 53B-17-201](http://www.le.utah.gov/UtahCode/getCodeSection?code=53B-17-201) establishes a Rehabilitation Center from the revenues from the trust fund to be used to serve disabled miners.
